content: 1. The coordination of inter-ministerial efforts is essential to ensure a unified approach to pandemic vaccine deployment and governance. This includes collaboration among stakeholders and partners to streamline operations and decision-making processes. 2. Drafting operational guidelines for vaccine rollout is critical. These guidelines must include governance frameworks and accountability measures to ensure transparency and efficiency in vaccine distribution. 3. Developing and verifying micro-plans is a necessary step to ensure that vaccine distribution is tailored to local needs and logistical realities. 4. Promoting equitable vaccine distribution and fair allocation is a priority. This involves supportive supervision to address disparities and ensure that vaccines reach all populations, especially those in underserved areas. 5. Adverse Event Following Immunization (AEFI) management, including causality assessment, is a key component of vaccine safety monitoring. This ensures that any adverse reactions are promptly identified, investigated, and addressed. 6. Surveillance of disease and vaccination coverage, along with reporting to the World Health Organization (WHO), is essential for tracking progress and identifying gaps in immunization efforts. 7. Oversight of program reviews, including post-introduction evaluations and lessons learned, is necessary to refine strategies and improve future pandemic responses. 8. Implementing corrective actions based on program reviews ensures that identified weaknesses are addressed promptly and effectively. 9. National civil society organizations play a vital role in advocacy and community engagement to support the uptake of pandemic vaccines. Their efforts help build trust and address vaccine hesitancy. 10. Planning and implementing pandemic vaccination campaigns require needs-based support for vaccination teams, particularly in areas with high levels of vaccine hesitancy. 11. Monitoring field activities designed to promote equitable vaccine allocation is crucial to ensure that distribution efforts are fair and inclusive. 12. International partner organizations provide technical assistance to countries in drafting National Deployment and Vaccination Plans (NDVPs) and operational guidelines for vaccine rollout. They also prepare training materials, train trainers, and conduct independent monitoring of field activities. 13. The private sector contributes expertise in research and development (R&D), supports cold chain and dry storage infrastructure, and engages in community outreach to raise awareness and address vaccine hesitancy. 14. The guidance document aims to facilitate the development and implementation of NDVPs for pandemic preparedness and response, particularly for respiratory viruses like pandemic influenza. 15. It enables the creation of national strategies for accessing pandemic vaccines and compiles lessons learned from COVID-19 and previous influenza pandemics. 16. The document serves as a comprehensive reference for preparedness and response activities, including emergency vaccination efforts. 17. The NDVP defines strategies and plans for the deployment, timely rollout, and monitoring of pandemic vaccination efforts. It acts as a single reference document for all stakeholders involved. 18. The guidance document comprises 16 chapters, each addressing specific aspects of pandemic preparedness. It includes key take-home messages and resources to aid countries in deploying, implementing, and monitoring pandemic vaccines. 19. The document also includes a template to help countries draft their NDVPs and a compilation of lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic. 20. The NDVP development process involves four core phases: inception, development, adoption, and continuous elaboration. These phases ensure a systematic approach to planning and implementation. 21. The inception phase includes establishing a multidisciplinary planning committee, conducting a situation analysis, and developing a work plan. 22. The development phase involves drafting, discussing, and consolidating the plan, including mapping roles of stakeholders and partner agencies. 23. The adoption phase includes testing the plan through simulation exercises, reviewing and finalizing the content, and obtaining government approval. 24. The continuous elaboration phase focuses on embedding preparedness into health systems, conducting regular simulation exercises, and updating the plan based on lessons learned. 25. The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of swift regulatory approval for vaccines and the need for robust systems to monitor vaccine safety and efficacy. 26. Seasonal influenza programs can provide valuable data to inform national strategic needs and assumptions for pandemic preparedness, including stockpiling medical countermeasures. 27. Innovations in vaccine research, such as mRNA-based platforms, offer advantages like shorter synthesis timelines and the potential for combination vaccines targeting multiple pathogens. 28. Expanding pandemic influenza vaccine production capacities is critical to addressing equity gaps and ensuring timely access to vaccines during a pandemic. 29. Global preparedness solutions must include early detection of new pathogens, flexible supply chains, scalable manufacturing processes, and optimized regulatory pathways. 30. The 100-day response ambition aims to develop and deploy medical countermeasures that meet safety, quality, and efficacy standards within a short timeframe. NDVPs can support this goal by enabling systematic planning and testing for the rapid introduction of novel vaccines.
